name: pi-dock
description: Your real Pi TUI in a VS Code sidebar view. No bundled agent, no native modules: VS Code shows a web page, ttyd turns your pi command into one.

piDock.command.markdownDescription: The command Pi Dock runs in the sidebar, as an argument list. Example: `["pi", "-c"]` continues your most recent session if Pi itself was stopped. With dtach installed (see `piDock.persist`) the process survives moving the view and reloading the window, so `-c` is rarely needed.

piDock.resume.markdownDescription: Start Pi on the conversation it was in when the window last closed or reloaded (`--session`), for this workspace folder. **Pi Dock: New Session** starts a fresh one and forgets the old. Off means every window start is a new conversation.

piDock.persist.markdownDescription: Keep Pi running when the view is moved or the window reloads, by running it under [dtach](https://github.com/crigler/dtach). Needs `dtach` installed; without it Pi starts over each time and a one-time warning says so.

piDock.dtachPath.description: Path to the dtach executable. Leave as "dtach" to use the one on your PATH.

piDock.ttydPath.description: Path to the ttyd executable. Leave as "ttyd" to use the one on your PATH.

piDock.fontSize.markdownDescription: Terminal font size in pixels. Empty uses `terminal.integrated.fontSize`.

piDock.fontFamily.description: Terminal font family. Empty uses terminal.integrated.fontFamily, then editor.fontFamily. Fonts that are not installed are skipped.

piDock.theme.markdownDescription: xterm.js colours that override single entries of the theme read live from your VS Code color theme, e.g. `{"background": "#181818"}`. Empty follows VS Code's terminal colors exactly.

piDock.clientOptions.markdownDescription: Extra [xterm.js options](https://xtermjs.org/docs/api/terminal/interfaces/iterminaloptions/) applied last, e.g. `{"scrollback": 5000, "cursorBlink": true}`. Read when the view opens.

piDock.escapeActions.markdownDescription: VS Code commands whose keyboard shortcuts leave the terminal for VS Code while it has focus. Pi Dock looks up the chords in VS Code's own keybindings (defaults, your `keybindings.json`, and extensions), so rebinding a command in VS Code moves its escape with it, and two-step chords work. Everything not bound to a listed command goes to Pi. The default gives you the command palette (F1, Ctrl+Shift+P), which costs Pi its backward model cycle, and Pi Dock's own toggle (Ctrl+Alt+P), which costs nothing Pi uses. See the README for the Pi keys other common commands would take.

piDock.extraArgs.description: Extra arguments passed to ttyd before the built-in ones.

walkthroughs.title: Set up Pi Dock
walkthroughs.description: Three programs on your PATH, then the sidebar. Check again says what is still missing; mark a step done once it is there.

steps.title: Install ttyd
steps.description:
Serves your pi command as a terminal the sidebar can draw.
[Check again](command:piDock.checkSetup)

steps.title: Install dtach
steps.description:
Keeps Pi running when the sidebar moves. Optional.
[Check again](command:piDock.checkSetup)

steps.title: Install Pi
steps.description:
So that ``pi`` works in a terminal, or point ``piDock.command`` at it.
[Check again](command:piDock.checkSetup)

steps.title: Open the sidebar
steps.description:
Click the π icon, or press Ctrl+Alt+P.
[Open Pi](command:piDock.focus)
